samples.summary:
Share-link mounts attach presence without a `name`, so attribution from that path is always empty — including for logged-in users. The design doc's premise is wrong.

`YorkieNoteStore.localAuthorName()` reads `doc.getMyPresence()?.name`. The only place that sets `name` is `notes-detail.tsx:259` (the owner's route). The share-link path builds `const presence = { username, email, photo }` (shared-document.tsx:837-841) with no `name` field at all, so every edit made through an *editor* share link records `author: ''` and renders as "Anonymous" — even when the editor is an authenticated user with a username. The new design-doc subsection asserts the opposite: "The name comes from the client's own presence `name`, which anonymous share-link editors already attach as `\"Anonymous\"`" (docs/design/notes/notes.md, new subsection). That claim does not hold in the tree, and the acceptance criterion "each line shows the author of its most recent edit" silently fails for the whole share-link editing surface.
samples.evidence: shared-document.tsx:837 `const presence = { username: currentUser?.username || "Anonymous", email: ..., photo: ... }` — no `name`; notes-detail.tsx:259 `name: currentUser.username` is the only writer of `name`.

samples.summary:
Design doc overstates the opt-in: attribution attributes are written on every insert regardless of the toggle.

The new subsection says a reader who never turns the gutter on gets "none of the per-edit bookkeeping", but `YorkieNoteStore.editText` unconditionally attaches `{ a, t }` to every insertion whether or not `showAuthors` is on — so every note in the product now pays the per-run attribute cost on the wire and in the CRDT, for all users. The behaviour may well be the intended design (attribution has to accrue before anyone can view it), but the doc as written misdescribes it and should say so plainly.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts editText: `if (insert.length > 0) root.content.edit(from, to, insert, { a: ..., t: Date.now() })` — no showAuthors gate.

finding.summary:
Share-link mounts attach presence without a `name`, so attribution from that path is always empty — including for logged-in users. The design doc's premise is wrong.

`YorkieNoteStore.localAuthorName()` reads `doc.getMyPresence()?.name`. The only place that sets `name` is `notes-detail.tsx:259` (the owner's route). The share-link path builds `const presence = { username, email, photo }` (shared-document.tsx:837-841) with no `name` field at all, so every edit made through an *editor* share link records `author: ''` and renders as "Anonymous" — even when the editor is an authenticated user with a username. The new design-doc subsection asserts the opposite: "The name comes from the client's own presence `name`, which anonymous share-link editors already attach as `\"Anonymous\"`" (docs/design/notes/notes.md, new subsection). That claim does not hold in the tree, and the acceptance criterion "each line shows the author of its most recent edit" silently fails for the whole share-link editing surface.
finding.evidence: shared-document.tsx:837 `const presence = { username: currentUser?.username || "Anonymous", email: ..., photo: ... }` — no `name`; notes-detail.tsx:259 `name: currentUser.username` is the only writer of `name`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the share-link mount attaches presence with no `name`, so share-link edits always record an empty author. Counterexample: shared-document.tsx:883-893, the `resolved.type === "note"` branch, does not pass the bare `presence` object — it spreads it and explicitly adds `name: presence.username` at line 890 (plus `color`, `selection`, `cursor`). With `presence.username = currentUser?.username || "Anonymous"` (line 838), a logged-in share-link editor attaches their real username and an anonymous one attaches "Anonymous" — exactly what `YorkieNoteStore.localAuthorName()` reads via `doc.getMyPresence()?.name` (yorkie-note-store.ts:135) and exactly what the design-doc sentence the finding calls false asserts. notes-detail.tsx:259 is therefore not the only writer of `name`. The base object at 837-841 lacking `name` is used unmodified only for the doc/slides/sheet branches, which do not use YorkieNoteStore, so it cannot affect note attribution. Both premises fail, so the derived acceptance-criterion failure does not follow.
